newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Sino-U.S. trade friction not serious for HK -Tsang.
newsitem.headline: Sino-U.S. trade friction not serious for HK -Tsang.

text.p: Hong Kong's Financial Secretary said on Monday that a trade dispute between China and the United States, while worrying, was unlikely to have any serious impact on the territory.
"We are obviously concerned but looking at the products under dispute, the direct trade impact is not likely to be serious," Donald Tsang told reporters.

Beijing said over the weekend it would suspend temporarily its imports of some U.S. textiles, farm goods and alcoholic beverages in retaliation for Washington's imposition of punitive charges on American purchases of Chinese textiles.

Beijing's temporary import ban would take effect on December 10. In September, Washington announced the punitive charges against import quotas for Chinese textile goods, accusing China of using transshipments to avoid U.S. quota restrictions.
But Tsang acknowledged that the trade dispute would not benefit Hong Kong either.
"China and the USA are respectively Hong Kong's largest trading partners, so any trade dispute between the two major partners is not likely to bring any benefits to Hong Kong," he said.
"I just hope that this dispute will be resolved satisfactorily without any further escalation."
China said on Monday it expected talks with the United States soon over the dispute.
